text:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm experimenting with thermal-aware page prioritization to reduce GPU throttling on multi-tenant nodes. rough idea below.
Kevin: nice, can you sketch how it interacts with eviction? sounds like extra churn risk.
Maya: plan is a priority score per page = hotness * (1 - thermal_penalty). thermal_penalty derived from per-GPU sensor rolling avg. lower score => earlier demote/evict.
Sophie: how do we get thermal signal? driver? node-exporter?
Maya: we can use hwmon via node-exporter + new /metrics gpu_thermal_celsius, or NVML if available. prototype uses nvml temp gauge.
Li: does this affect SLA? if we start moving pages proactively we might spike miss rates.
Maya: yep — we'll gate by latency SLO. if p99>target then disable proactive thermal demote.
Dave: what about cross-GPU migration cost? moving pages between GPUs for thermal balancing could be expensive.
Maya: config knobs: max_migrations_per_sec, cost_threshold (ms per page), prefer-host-staging if migration cost > threshold.
Kevin: interface: allocator should expose 'thermal_score_hint(page_id, score)' and accept 'migration_budget' from the scheduler. keep allocator orthogonal.
Maya: exactly. that keeps eviction decision local but allows global scheduling to throttle migrations.
infra-bot: deploy succeeded: canary on cluster infer-12 with thermal probe enabled
Sophie: metrics to track: temp_celsius, p99_latency, page_migrations/sec, kvcache_hit, demote_rate.
Li: add a safety: if demote_rate correlates with model quality regressions, auto rollback.
Maya: agreed — we'll wire quality monitoring (eval set) as a kill switch.
Dave: curious about fragmentation: selective demote of frequently accessed compressed pages might fragment host memory.
Maya: thinking of a compact phase: on low-load windows run host-compactor to defrag staging pool.
Kevin: timeline? can we get experiment in canary today and run A/B for 48h?
Maya: I can roll a canary with nvml probes and a basic hint interface. target: observe migration cost and p99 impact.
Sophie: ping me if you need eval harness for regression detection.
Kevin: file an RFC or an RFC-followup note with the allocation API signature and safety knobs.
Maya: will do. drafting now — putting details in /docs/thermal-prio.md and will link back here.
Li: nit: use percentile-based thermal_penalty (90th) to avoid transient spikes.
Maya: good call. that'll smooth out reaction.
Kevin: :thumbsup: 
Maya: thanks all — will update thread with RFC link and canary results later.
